content.comment_body: Hello! I have a [product_name] program using various multifunctional switches and network inputs. I need to transfer the status of these switches into a recipe menu on an HMI panel, so the statuses are selectable. What is the best way to do this? I prefer not to modify the main [product_name] program; is there a simpler approach? Thanks in advance for your help.
Could you clarify what you mean by HMI? Are you referring to an HMI panel?
There is an example available on the [company_name] website: [url]. It describes HMI communication starting from [product_name] V11.x (TIA Portal).
I'm working on a system with [product_name] and an HMI panel; we just need to add a recipe menu to the HMI. The suggested link does not seem to address my issue.

To use network inputs and outputs, they are handled directly through Ethernet communication between the HMI and the [product_name]. Here is a table (in Dutch) showing address mapping. In the Help menu of [product_name] programming software, you can find the same address details. For example, fixed addresses and block types including VM, I, AI, Q, AQ, M, AM, NI, NAI, NQ, and NAQ are listed with their respective address ranges and sizes. Refer to the documentation for detailed address mapping and integration information.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for a way to integrate switch status data from a [product_name] into a recipe menu on an HMI panel. Their main challenge is generating the data transfer without modifying the existing [product_name] program logic. Provided examples and links have not resolved the issue, and current documentation seems either incomplete or language-specific.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward solution for transferring switch statuses to the HMI recipe menu without changing the core [product_name] program. They hope to receive clear instructions or relevant working examples.
